title: Multiplication Tables: Times Table Chart - GeeksforGeeks
content:
Multiplication table is the list of multiples from 1 to 10 of a number. It is a table in which the multiple of a number is represented. Thus the multiplication table contains the first 10 multiples of the various numbers. This multiplication table is also called the times table and is widely used for simplification purposes.

Let's learn more about Multiplication tables from 1 to 20, its chart, examples, in detail below.

What is Multiplication Table?

A multiplication table is a chart that shows the product of two numbers. Usually, one set of numbers is written on the left column and another set is written on the top-most row. Having a multiplication chart saves a considerable amount of time and energy in doing calculations. A multiplication table is a fundamental mathematical table that helps learners understand and memorize the results of multiplying two numbers together.

Table Calculator

The multiplication table calculator prepared at GeeksforGeeks is added below and is used to easily generate the table of any natural number.

Multiplication Table Chart 1 to 20

Multiplication Tables from 1 to 20 are the tables that are very important for the students to learn and are used by them for various purposes, it helps students to simplify mathematical problems, ease the calculation, and solve various problems.

Multiplication tables also called, times tables are very useful and they are discussed in groups of two from 1 to 10 and 11 to 20.

Multiplication Chart

Multiplication Chart is a chart that contains the multiplication tables the multiplication chart is very important and is useful for learning tables in a quick and easy format. The chart contains the table from 1 to 20 and is very useful for memorizing the table.

For the convenience of the students, the chart is divided into two parts that contain tables from 1 to 10 and tables from 11 to 20. Let's learn about both in detail.

Multiplication Chart From 1 to 10

Times table chart 1 to 10 or the multiplication chart 1 to 10 is the chart that contains tables from 1 to 10 in a tabular format. In the table, the first row contains all the numbers for which we have to write the table i.e. the number from 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, and 10 and the first column contains the numbers for which the multiplication table is found, i.e. 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, and 10. Then each column in the table contains the product of the number from the corresponding first row and first column.

Multiplication Chart From 11 to 20

Times table chart 11 to 20 or the multiplication chart 11 to 20 is the chart that contains tables from 11 to 20 in a tabular format. In the table, the first row contains all the numbers for which we have to write the table i.e. the number from 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17, 18, 19, and 20 and the first column contains the numbers for which the multiplication table is found, i.e. 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, and 10. Then each column in the table contains the product of the number from the corresponding first row and first column.

Importance of Multiplication Table

The multiplication tables are very important and they are very useful for solving various problems and are very helpful in simplifying mathematical problems. The multiplication tables solve the mathematical calculation and make problem-solving in math's very easy.

These tables are also used for solving and simplifying various real-life problems also. Suppose Karan is given 6 rupees every day for a week then the total amount he has after one week is calculated using the concept of the table as,

Karan gets Rupees = 6 Rupees daily for a week.

Total Amount after one week = 6×7 = 42 rupees (Using Table of 6)

Thus, tables are very useful for solving various problems in real-life also. These tables help us to quickly solve problems and find the solution very quickly.

How to Memorize Multiplication Tables

Learning tables are very important for students to perform well in their classes. So we have suggested some points that will help the students to learn the table easily.

  • Read multiplication tables multiple times loudly to learn the table easily.
  • Write multiplication tables multiple times to learn the table easily.
  • Find various patterns in the multiplication table and learn that table using that pattern.
  • Table of two only has even numbers.
  • Table of 10 and 20 are easy to remember as they are only tables 1 and 2 with 0 at their end.
  • Table of 5 only has 0, 5 in its unit place, etc.

Multiplication Tables Examples

Some examples related to multiplication tables from 1 to 20 are

Example 1: Abhay eats 2 eggs a day, how many eggs did he eat in a month?

Solution: 

Abhay eats eggs in a day = 2 eggs

Number of days in a month = 30 days

Total eggs eaten by Abhay in a month = 2 × 30  (Using the table of 2) = 60 eggs

Thus, Abhay eats 60 eggs in a Month

Example 2: Babu earns 5 rupees a day, then how much did he earn in a week?

Solution:

Babu earns in a day = 5 rupees

Number of days in a week = 7 days

Babu earns in a week = 5 × 7  (Using the table of 5) = 35 rupees

Thus, Babu earns 35 rupees in a week.

Example 3: Simplify

  • 9 × 4 = 
  • 7 × 7 = 
  • 8 × 6 =

Solution: 

Using multiplication table we get,

  • 9 × 4 = 36
  • 7 × 7 = 49
  • 8 × 6 = 48

Example 4: Simplify

  • 19 × 5 =
  • 17 × 3 =
  • 18 × 6 =

Solution: 

Using multiplication table we get,

  • 19 × 5 = 95
  • 17 × 3 = 51
  • 18 × 6 = 108
